name: Wigner-Ville distribution (WVD)
domain: 车辆—轨道与基础结构动力学

complete_examples.text: The paper is organized as: (a) In Section 2, a time-frequency analysis approach is developed by effectively uniting the wavelet transform and Wigner-Ville distribution (WVD) to accurately extract the signal features in time-frequency domain; (b) A three-dimensional (3-D) nonlinear vehicle-track coupled model is programmed to numerically explore dynamic correlations between track irregularities and wheel/rail interaction forces; (c) Based on methodologies presented in Sections 2 and 3, the modeling procedures aiming at predicting track sections with deteriorated wheel/rail interactions will be illustrated in Section 4; (d) In Section 5, validations for the vehicle-track interaction model and the proposed time-frequency analysis method are presented accompanied by typical numerical examples.
The Wigner-Ville distribution (WVD) of a signal sðtÞ was firstly proposed by Wigner in the year of 1932, then Ville employed it into the signal processing.

To further investigate the effect of CDS-induced additional irregularity on the time-frequency characterization of car body accelerations, the Wigner-Ville distribution (WVD) of car body accelerations is calculated, as shown in Fig. 21.
